title: Degree of a discrete derivative
statement: Let $f\colon\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$, choose a coordinate $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $k$ be a natural number. If $f$ has Fourier degree at most $k$, then its discrete derivative in coordinate $i$, obtained by setting that coordinate to $1$ and $-1$ and taking half the difference, has Fourier degree at most $k-1$, with subtraction truncated at zero.
hypotheses_covered: The Fourier degree of $f$ is at most $k$
